main_facts: METR explains how external AI-risk work can inform the public without pretending to certify deployment decisions. It commits to disclose project scope, access limits, redactions, constraints and conflicts, while protecting confidential material. The organization also aims to publish evidence and methods for outside analysis, acknowledge scientific uncertainty and issue iterative findings rather than closed-door assurance.

When reading an AI safety assessment, check who paid, what evaluators could access, which evidence was removed, how methods can be challenged and whether conclusions exceed the scope. These disclosures help leaders distinguish independent evidence from a broad safety endorsement.

main_facts: LangChain describes five Deep Agents mechanisms for limiting context rot: offload large inputs to files, summarize older turns, load skills only when relevant, isolate noisy work in subagents and persist selected knowledge as plain Markdown. Summaries remain recoverable, and user-controlled storage lets memory survive a model or provider change instead of remaining trapped in one service.

Keep active context small without deleting evidence. Store raw outputs behind previews, preserve summarized history for retrieval, separate exploratory work and review persistent memory edits. This makes long-running agents easier to audit, migrate and correct when their retained assumptions become stale.
